acceptance.criterion_verbatim: After a correct password on an MFA-enabled account, the browser shows a prompt asking whether to send a code -- and NO code is sent until the user confirms. Both halves: the prompt renders, AND no send occurs before the click.
acceptance.invocation: Portal served at localhost:5175 from 087a456f, headless Chromium. window.fetch overridden to return ONLY the /auth/login shape the deployed handler already emits (index.ts:166): HTTP 200 {mfaRequired:true, challengeId, channel:'email'}, no accessToken, no refresh cookie. Login form filled and submitted; screenshot taken and READ. Separately: auth-handler/src/{index,auth,mfa}.ts read at source.
acceptance.output_evidence: FIRST HALF PASSES -- the prompt renders. Observed body text: 'Two-step verification / This account uses a one-time code. Choose where to receive it, then confirm below -- nothing is sent until you do.' Screenshot READ at .playwright-mcp/page-2026-09-01T02-18-01-368Z.png. SECOND HALF CANNOT PASS: auth.ts:93-95 calls issueChallenge() then sendMfaCodeEmail() INSIDE login(), before the response returns. All 16 routes of index.ts read; mfa.ts exports exactly two operations; issueChallenge has exactly ONE call site, inside login(). There is no endpoint that issues or sends a challenge independently of /auth/login, so the mail has already gone before any browser can render this prompt. Exercised with POST /auth/mfa/send ABSENT (stubbed 404, the gateway's real answer today): the failure is SHOWN -- 'Could not send the code. Please try again.' -- the flow does NOT advance, and nothing reports a code as sent. Screenshot READ at .playwright-mcp/page-2026-09-01T02-18-16-991Z.png.
acceptance.denominator: 16 of 16 routes in index.ts read; 2 of 2 mfa.ts exported operations enumerated; 1 of 1 issueChallenge call sites.
acceptance.status_reason: BLOCKED BY THE BACKEND, and NOT scored on its satisfied half -- the row is a conjunction. The prompt renders; the no-send-before-confirm half is unsatisfiable by ANY frontend against today's handler, because issuance is welded inside login(). requestMfaCode() is already wired to POST /auth/mfa/send, so the row passes with NO further frontend change once issuance is split out. Proposed owner 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z (rule 13 puts infra there); routed to 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z as msg 17360. This is Andrew's literal complaint -- 'not just send silently without a UI flow' IS this line -- so passing the row on the rendered prompt alone would satisfy the letter while shipping the thing he objected to. INSTRUMENT LIMIT, stated not implied: the auth responses are stubbed at window.fetch, so every browser row here exercises THE CLIENT from the fetch boundary inward, NOT the integrated system. It cannot show the server emits these shapes -- that is a source read, and three seats performing it is three seats on ONE rung, which is repetition rather than corroboration.

'Sends nothing' holds for the right reason: cancelling only discards component state and issues no request. handleCancelMfa deliberately does NOT call logout() -- calling it would imply a session had existed, and on the MFA branch login() establishes none.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: NEGATIVE: no path in the new UI reveals whether an account exists or whether MFA is enabled on it, beyond what the pre-existing login already reveals.

acceptance.output_evidence: The opt-in prompt and the challenge screen render ONLY when login() returns mfaRequired, which the handler emits only after verifyPassword() succeeds -- so both are reachable only by a caller who already holds the correct password. The credential-form failure path is untouched: the handler still throws one generic 'Invalid email or password' for a non-existent account and a wrong password alike, and records an attempt on the same throttle key in both branches. This change adds no new pre-authentication branch and no new request before the password check.
acceptance.denominator: 3 of 3 render branches added (credentials, optin, challenge); 0 new pre-auth network calls -- requestMfaCode and verifyMfa both run strictly after a successful password.
acceptance.status_reason: BOUNDED: this is a code-path argument plus the observed absence of any new pre-auth request. It is NOT a timing measurement. I did not measure response-time differentials between existing and non-existent accounts; that is a handler property and is unchanged by this commit, and I say so rather than let 'PASS' imply I measured it.
